# Known differences from NSubstitute

<!-- Generated by test/NSubstituteComparison.Specs. Run the specs with VERIFICATIONGLUE_ACCEPT_DIFFERENCES=1 to update it. -->

VerificationGlue.Mocks behaves like NSubstitute 6.2.0 in 40 of 48 comparison cases. This page lists the other 8 and the reason for each. The [migration guide](migrate-from-nsubstitute.md) shows how to move a test project.

Each case is one source file that compiles against both libraries. Only the `using` directives and `Mock.Of<T>()` change. `test/NSubstituteComparison.Specs` runs every case under both libraries in CI. It fails when a case differs without a recorded reason, when a recorded difference no longer differs, and when this page differs from the run.

| Area | Cases | Differences |
|---|---|---|
| [Argument matching](../../test/NSubstituteComparison/Cases/Matching.cs) | 12 | 3 |
| [Setup precedence](../../test/NSubstituteComparison/Cases/Precedence.cs) | 9 | 0 |
| [Response sequences](../../test/NSubstituteComparison/Cases/Sequences.cs) | 6 | 0 |
| [Async results](../../test/NSubstituteComparison/Cases/AsyncResults.cs) | 8 | 1 |
| [Last-call hazards](../../test/NSubstituteComparison/Cases/LastCall.cs) | 8 | 2 |
| [Parallel use](../../test/NSubstituteComparison/Cases/Parallel.cs) | 5 | 2 |
| Total | 48 | 8 |

The comparison is bounded to these areas. It does not cover members that only one library has, such as NSubstitute's `ReturnsForAnyArgs` and `Received.InOrder`.

## Argument matching

### A matcher after an argument that holds the default value

VerificationGlue.Mocks gives each matcher the argument it is written at, which a generated interceptor reads from the source. NSubstitute cannot tell which of the two zero arguments the matcher stands for.

```cs
var calc = Mock.Of<ICalculator>();
observe.Try("Add(0, Arg.Any<int>()).Returns(5)", () => calc.Add(0, Arg.Any<int>()).Returns(5));

observe.Record("Add(0, 9)", calc.Add(0, 9));
observe.Record("Add(9, 0)", calc.Add(9, 0));
```

| Observation | NSubstitute | VerificationGlue.Mocks |
|---|---|---|
| `Add(0, Arg.Any<int>()).Returns(5)` | `throws AmbiguousArgumentsException` | `ok` |
| `Add(0, 9)` | `0` | `5` |
| `Add(9, 0)` | `0` | `0` |

### A matcher before an argument that holds the default value

VerificationGlue.Mocks gives each matcher the argument it is written at. NSubstitute rejects the setup, because the 0 in the second argument could also be the value a matcher returned.

```cs
var calc = Mock.Of<ICalculator>();
observe.Try("Add(Arg.Any<int>(), 0).Returns(5)", () => calc.Add(Arg.Any<int>(), 0).Returns(5));

observe.Record("Add(9, 0)", calc.Add(9, 0));
observe.Record("Add(9, 1)", calc.Add(9, 1));
```

| Observation | NSubstitute | VerificationGlue.Mocks |
|---|---|---|
| `Add(Arg.Any<int>(), 0).Returns(5)` | `throws AmbiguousArgumentsException` | `ok` |
| `Add(9, 0)` | `0` | `5` |
| `Add(9, 1)` | `0` | `0` |

### An array argument that is not params matches the same values in a new array

VerificationGlue.Mocks compares every array argument by its elements. NSubstitute does that only for a params argument, and compares other arrays by reference.

```cs
var calc = Mock.Of<ICalculator>();
calc.Count(new[] { 1, 2 }).Returns(2);

observe.Record("Count(new[] { 1, 2 })", calc.Count(new[] { 1, 2 }));
```

| Observation | NSubstitute | VerificationGlue.Mocks |
|---|---|---|
| `Count(new[] { 1, 2 })` | `0` | `2` |

## Async results

### A setup whose value comes from an await

VerificationGlue.Mocks keeps the last call in an AsyncLocal, so it follows the setup across the await. NSubstitute keeps it per thread, so a setup whose await resumes on another thread loses its call.

```cs
var calc = Mock.Of<ICalculator>();

await observe.TryAsync("Add(1, 2).Returns(await LoadOnAnotherThread(10))", async () => calc.Add(1, 2).Returns(await LoadOnAnotherThread(10)));

observe.Record("Add(1, 2)", calc.Add(1, 2));
```

| Observation | NSubstitute | VerificationGlue.Mocks |
|---|---|---|
| `Add(1, 2).Returns(await LoadOnAnotherThread(10))` | `throws CouldNotSetReturnDueToNoLastCallException` | `ok` |
| `Add(1, 2)` | `0` | `10` |

## Last-call hazards

### Returns with no mock call before it

Both libraries reject the setup, with different exception types. VerificationGlue.Mocks also reports VGM0005 at build time for a Returns on a value that is not a mock call.

```cs
var mock = Mock.Of<ICalculator>();
observe.Try("5.Returns(6)", () => 5.Returns(6));
observe.Record("Add(0, 0)", mock.Add(0, 0));
```

| Observation | NSubstitute | VerificationGlue.Mocks |
|---|---|---|
| `5.Returns(6)` | `throws CouldNotSetReturnDueToNoLastCallException` | `throws MockSetupException` |
| `Add(0, 0)` | `0` | `0` |

### An abandoned Arg matcher before an unrelated call

Both libraries fail the next call and then clear the matcher, with different exception types. VerificationGlue.Mocks also reports VGM0002 at build time for a matcher that is not an argument of a mock call.

```cs
var calc = Mock.Of<ICalculator>();
Arg.Any<string>();

observe.TryValue("Add(1, 2)", () => calc.Add(1, 2));
observe.TryValue("Add(1, 2) again", () => calc.Add(1, 2));
```

| Observation | NSubstitute | VerificationGlue.Mocks |
|---|---|---|
| `Add(1, 2)` | `throws RedundantArgumentMatcherException` | `throws AmbiguousArgumentsException` |
| `Add(1, 2) again` | `0` | `0` |

## Parallel use

### 200 parallel setups whose values come from an await

VerificationGlue.Mocks binds every setup to its own call, because the last call follows each setup across its await. Under NSubstitute every setup resumes on a new thread with no last call, and fails.

```cs
var calc = Mock.Of<ICalculator>();
var failed = 0;

await Task.WhenAll(Enumerable.Range(0, 200).Select(i => Task.Run(async () =>
{
    try
    {
        calc.Add(i, i).Returns(await AsyncResults.LoadOnAnotherThread(i * 10));
    }
    catch (Exception)
    {
        Interlocked.Increment(ref failed);
    }
})));

observe.Record("setups that threw", failed);
observe.Record("calls that return their setup", Enumerable.Range(0, 200).Count(i => calc.Add(i, i) == i * 10));
```

| Observation | NSubstitute | VerificationGlue.Mocks |
|---|---|---|
| `setups that threw` | `200` | `0` |
| `calls that return their setup` | `1` | `200` |

### A setup finished in a child task

A child task starts with its parent's last call in VerificationGlue.Mocks, so the setup binds. NSubstitute keeps the last call per thread, so the child task has none.

```cs
var calc = Mock.Of<ICalculator>();
var call = calc.Add(1, 2);

await observe.TryAsync("call.Returns(3) in a child task", () => Task.Factory.StartNew(() => call.Returns(3), TaskCreationOptions.LongRunning));
observe.Record("Add(1, 2)", calc.Add(1, 2));
```

| Observation | NSubstitute | VerificationGlue.Mocks |
|---|---|---|
| `call.Returns(3) in a child task` | `throws CouldNotSetReturnDueToNoLastCallException` | `ok` |
| `Add(1, 2)` | `0` | `3` |
